title: Composition of finite-type relatively ample morphisms over a quasi-compact base
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], both of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and suppose $S$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Suppose there exist an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $L$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $M$ [def-sc-invertible-module] that are respectively $f$-relatively ample and $g$-relatively ample. Then $g\circ f$ is of finite type and there exists an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $N$ that is $(g\circ f)$-relatively ample. Here an invertible module $L$ on the source of a morphism $h$ is $h$-relatively ample if $h$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and, for every affine open $V$ of its target, $L|_{h^{-1}(V)}$ is ample in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Tag 0C4M (lemma-composition-quasi-projective), with Definition Tag 01VW(1) (definition-quasi-projective) and Definition Tag 01VH (definition-relatively-ample).

proof.text: Choose witnesses $L,M$ to the two relative-ampleness hypotheses. Apply [lem-sfb-composition-finite-affine-twist-bounds] to $f,g,L,M$, using the affine-open ampleness conditions in those hypotheses. Obtain $h=g\circ f$ of finite type and quasi-compact, a finite affine covering $(V_i)_{1\leq i\leq r}$ of $S$, the restricted data $f_i,L_i,M_i$, and bounds $a_i\geq0$ for which every twist $L_i\otimes f_i^*(M_i^{\otimes a})$ with $a\geq a_i$ is ample.

source.place: Tag 0C4K (lemma-ample-composition), finite affine-cover reduction and local application of Tag 0892(1) (lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample); finite type uses Tags 01T3 and 01T4; relative ampleness is Definition 01VH.

proof.text: Choose one nonnegative integer bound a_i for every member of the finite cover and put a = sum_i a_i. Nonnegativity of all the summands implies a_i <= a for every i. Thus every local twist at exponent a is ample by Step 1. The sum is nonnegative, so its natural-number exponent a.toNat is exactly a. For an empty covering the empty sum is zero; no nonempty-index hypothesis or infinite maximum is used.

source.place: Tag 0C4K (lemma-ample-composition), finite affine-cover reduction and local application of Tag 0892(1) (lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample); finite type uses Tags 01T3 and 01T4; relative ampleness is Definition 01VH.

proof.text: Set $N=L\otimes f^*(M^{\otimes a})$. Apply [lem-sfb-invertible-twist-open-restriction] to $f,L,M,a$ to obtain invertibility of $N$, including when the cover is empty. For each $i$, take $U=Y_i=g^{-1}(V_i)$ in its open-restriction assertion. It identifies $N|_{X_i}$ with $L_i\otimes f_i^*(M_i^{\otimes a})$, including at $a=0$. Its ampleness equivalence and Step 2 imply that $N|_{X_i}$ is ample for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 0C4K (lemma-ample-composition), identifying the restriction of the displayed global twist with the local twist. Module comparisons: Modules Tags 01CD (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), 0B8L (lemma-pullback-invertible), 01CT (lemma-constructions-invertible); Sheaves Tag 0097 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules).

proof.text: For each $i$, $h^{-1}(V_i)=f^{-1}(g^{-1}(V_i))=X_i$, so Step 3 gives ampleness of $N|_{h^{-1}(V_i)}$. Apply [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-affine-cover] to the quasi-compact map $h$, the globally invertible module $N$ and the affine cover $(V_i)$. It gives ampleness of $N|_{h^{-1}(V)}$ for every affine open $V\subseteq S$. Together with quasi-compactness this is precisely $h$-relative ampleness. Use this $N$ as the existential witness; finite type of $h$ was obtained in Step 1. If the cover is empty, $S$, $Y$ and $X$ are empty; Step 3 still supplies the global invertible witness and the criterion applies to the empty cover.
